title: Agentops hybrid dispatch task packet
description: A frozen bounded implementation packet handed to one disposable OpenCode worker loop. The coordinator authors it; the worker never edits it.

schema_version.description: v1 packets remain readable for receipt/replay compatibility. New packets use v2, whose acceptance properties have stable ids.

task_id.description: Stable id for the packet. It becomes a branch component and a directory name under docs/evidence/receipts/, so it must be safe as a path segment: it starts alphanumeric, carries a hyphen-separated suffix, and admits no whitespace or separators. The first segment accepts lowercase and dots so a release-unit id such as 'v5.2-release-unit' is expressible -- the earlier ^[A-Z0-9]+- form rejected every one of them.

claim_actor.description: Actor holding the sprintctl claim. Always the coordinator, never the worker.

claim_id.description: Exact live claim id held by claim_actor for this packet.

starts_red.description: Command ids the coordinator asserts are RED at starting_commit, because the oracle for this packet is a test that does not pass yet. prepare requires exactly these to fail and every other registered command to pass: a starts_red command that is already green means the oracle does not discriminate, and the packet is refused rather than dispatched against a gate that cannot fail.

reference_patch.description: Optional repo-relative path (under docs/evidence/packets/ or similar) to a unified diff that is a reference solution. validate applies it at starting_commit in a throwaway checkout, rejects it if it touches anything outside writable_patch_paths, and requires every starts_red command to go green. Absent, the report records oracle_satisfiable_within_paths as skipped:no-reference, never true. A cheap-tier packet SHOULD carry one; it is mandatory once L-3 self_candidate is on for the class.

release_boundary.description: Marks the packet as crossing a release boundary. The L-1 driver refuses such a packet before any stage runs (L-2 stop condition 'release-boundary'); a release boundary is an owner touchpoint, not loop work.

supersedes.description: task_id of the failed packet this corrected retry replaces.

required_outcomes.description: Coordinator-authored outcomes, ordered. Addressable by stable INDEX in v0 -- position is the identity, so entries are appended rather than reordered or removed once a packet is frozen. Deliberately NOT promoted to objects with ids: unlike acceptance_properties, nothing downstream joins these to a gate, so an id would be ceremony that has to be kept unique for no consumer. Revisit if a comparison pass ever needs to address one across packets.

acceptance_properties.description: Coordinator-authored deterministic failure properties. Each relevant requirement needs a gate that fails when the requirement is ignored. v2 requires a packet-unique stable id.

non_goals.description: What this packet deliberately does not do, ordered. Addressable by stable INDEX in v0, on the same terms as required_outcomes, and deliberately not promoted to objects with ids for the same reason.

allowed_command_ids.description: Command ids resolved against the repository hybrid.commands map. Free-form shell is never granted.

context_churn.description: Coordinator-authored stall limits. These target repeated unchanged context and mutation-free churn, not cheap cache writes generally. Enforcement is harness-side when telemetry permits and otherwise recorded in the receipt.

gate_set.description: The ordered gate set for a release-unit packet, from pathway section 5. Order is load-bearing rather than decorative: a cold prepare that runs after the suite proves nothing, because the suite has already written to the tree it was meant to find clean. Produced by release_unit_packet.py so that no two sub-releases disagree about what 'gated' meant.

order.description: 1-based position in the pathway's gate order.

gate.description: Stable gate identifier a receipt and scorecard refer to later.

stop_conditions.description: The encoded L-2 stop conditions this packet is subject to, as stable identifiers. Carried explicitly on a release-unit packet so the orchestrator does not have to reconstruct them per sub-release.

debt.description: Refactors this packet defers, one line each. Rule 7 of the metanarrative brief requires a packet to carry one whenever it defers work; under owner constraint C-3 that is expected rather than a smell, and the accumulated list feeds the v5.9 refactor pass. In use since V5-M10b and undeclared here until 2026-08-24.

retry_context.description: Why this packet is being retried, carried into the worker's purpose. L-4 appends the prior gate's stdout_tail and stderr_tail here; the coordinator adds the prior attempts' dispositions, spend and diagnosed cause so a retry is not re-litigated from a transcript. Free-form by design -- the fields differ per failure -- so this object is deliberately not closed.

amendments.description: Coordinator amendments to a frozen packet, newest last. A packet is frozen at a commit, so a spec row that turns out to contradict another cannot simply be rewritten in place without the change becoming invisible; recording it here keeps the packet's history auditable against its receipt. In use since V5-M9 and undeclared here until 2026-08-24.

id.description: Packet-unique stable requirement identifier, for example REQ-001.
